core_claims.claim: Hyperscale datacom transceiver demand ramp is the core engine of Lumentum's revenue acceleration.
core_claims.why_core: Determines durability of top-line growth and valuation re-rating potential.
core_claims.strongest_support: Sequential revenue rose from $808.4M (Q3 FY26) to $1.01B (Q4 FY26).
core_claims.strongest_counter: Evidence lacks customer names, volumes, segment mix; ramp attribution is inferred.
core_claims.missing_evidence: Segment breakdown, customer identity, unit volumes, transceiver pricing.
core_claims.what_would_change_this_claim: Segment data showing growth from non-datacom lines or customer order cuts.

core_claims.claim: Volume scaling is delivering operating leverage and gross margin expansion.
core_claims.why_core: Margin trajectory determines whether revenue growth converts into earnings and multiple support.
core_claims.strongest_support: Q3 FY26 release cites GAAP gross margin alongside rising revenue.
core_claims.strongest_counter: Margin values truncated in evidence; expansion direction unverified.
core_claims.missing_evidence: Actual gross margin figures, cost structure, fab utilization data.
core_claims.what_would_change_this_claim: Disclosed margins flat or declining despite higher revenue.

core_claims.claim: Revenue is concentrated among few hyperscale cloud buyers, creating structural volatility risk.
core_claims.why_core: Concentration drives pricing pressure, order swings, and valuation discount risk.
core_claims.strongest_support: Unverified; no customer concentration data present in evidence.
core_claims.strongest_counter: Unverified; diversified customer base cannot be ruled out.
core_claims.missing_evidence: Customer concentration percentages, top-customer revenue disclosures.
core_claims.what_would_change_this_claim: Filings showing broad customer base or low top-customer concentration.

counter_reasoning.strongest_counter: Evidence is aggregate revenue only; no segment, customer, product, or volume data supports datacom attribution.
counter_reasoning.competing_hypothesis: Growth may stem from telecom components, chip/component sales to module makers, channel inventory build, or pricing.
counter_reasoning.most_likely_wrong: Attribution of the revenue acceleration specifically to hyperscale datacom transceiver demand; causality is inferred, not evidenced.
counter_reasoning.what_would_invalidate: Segment data showing non-datacom lines drove growth, or disclosed hyperscale customer order cuts or delays.
counter_reasoning.missing_evidence: Segment breakdown, customer identity, unit volumes, transceiver pricing, backlog, order patterns.
